newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen ends flat, cautious ahead of tankan.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen ends flat, cautious ahead of tankan.

text.p: June 13 settlement prev settlement
TIFFE Euroyen 3M (Z) 99.05 99.05

The key December three-month euroyen futures contract settled flat on Friday, as market players adopted a cautious stance ahead of release of Bank of Japan's key "tankan" corporate sentiment survey on June 25.
"Market players are still not sure whether or not the BOJ will raise rates within the year, and this made it hard to buy the December," a city bank trader said.
Turnover was 40,011 contracts.
Euroyen futures were sold briefly on SIMEX, after the close of Tokyo's day session in response to Japan's January-March gross domestic product data, traders said.
"The December fell as low as 99.03 on SIMEX, after the GDP figures came in stronger than expected," a trader for a major brokerage house said.
The December stood at 99.06 on SIMEX as of 0742 GMT.
Japan's GDP rose a real 1.6 percent in the January to March quarter from the previous quarter, or an annualised 6.6 percent, the Economic Planning Agency said on Friday.
The market had been expecting January-March GDP to grow by about four to five percent on an annualised basis.
On Monday, the market will be focusing on the release of revised industrial output data for April, traders said.
"There is a possibility that April output data could be revised upwards, and if that is the case, we may see some selling," the first trader said.
The government's preliminary figures released in May showed Japan's industrial output fell 0.4 percent in April.
The BOJ drained 200 billion yen from the money market on Friday morning offsetting the market's projected fund surplus.
The key overnight call rate was most actively traded at 0.43 percent, down from Thursday's weighted average of 0.46 percent, traders said.
The overnight call rate sank on Friday, as banks did not need to rush to pile up funds on the last day of the current bank reserve reporting period, traders said.
On Monday, the start of a new reporting period, the BOJ will probably conduct a neutral operation and try to gauge the market's sentiment, a trust bank trader said.
About 80 billion yen worth of key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.59 percent.
About 20 billion yen worth of one-month CDs were issued at 0.57 percent. Two-month CDs were offered at 0.58 percent.
Interest rate swap (IRS) rates rose briefly after the release of January-March GDP data, a trader for another city bank said.
But the effect was limited as the market is more interested in data for the April-June period than the January-March period, the trader said.
Three-year IRS rates were quoted at 1.50/54 percent as of 0812 GMT, down from 1.52/56 percent on Thursday. The 10-year IRS rate was at 2.83/87 percent, down from 2.86/90 percent.
